newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi defence minister in Bahrain.
newsitem.headline: Saudi defence minister in Bahrain.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's defence minister arrived in Bahrain on Wednesday on a visit that diplomats believed was linked to efforts to convince the emir to attend the next Gulf Arab summit in Qatar.
Prince Sultan arrived in Manama and went straight into talks with Sheikh Isa bin Sulman al-Khalifa, Gulf news agencies said.
Bahrain has threatened to boycott the December 7 Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) summit because of a territorial dispute with Qatar.
The emir told the Saudi prince Manama was committed to the six-nation GCC and praised Saudi efforts to boost the GCC, the agencies said.

Diplomats said the visit was part of a flurry of contacts by Gulf Arab officials to prepare for the summit of heads of state of Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman, Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates.
Saudi Arabia, the dominant power in the group, is trying to find a compromise to ensure full attendance at the summit.
Bahrain has said it would boycott the summit in protest against Qatar's failure to withdraw a case it has taken to the International Court of Justice over their territorial dispute.
Qatar said it would only withdraw the case if Saudi mediation succeeded in settling the long-standing row over a cluster of islands potentially rich in natural gas.
GCC Secretary-General Jameel Hujilan said after arriving in Kuwait on Tuesday -- the last leg of a regional tour ahead of the summit -- that all Gulf Arab leaders might attend.
Saudi Minister of State Abdul-Aziz bin Abdullah al-Khoweiter visited Doha for several hours on Wednesday, the official Saudi Press Agency said. It did not give details.
